description: Threat model claims and their pinning tests (docs/ARCHITECTURE.md §1.4, §3, §10, SECURITY.md, docs/GATES.md). tests/test_threat_model_claims.rs verifies that every named pinning test exists and tracks untested claims as targets for adversarial red-teaming.

claims.claim: The merge gate verdict: a change that erodes tests, safety comments or policy is blocked, or it lands with its waiver on record.
The policy (discipline.toml, CI workflows, action inputs, hook/sandbox settings, protected paths) is guarded against unauthorized weakening.
The record of waivers, loosenings and ratifications is preserved and auditable across history via discipline audit.
Repository hygiene prevents publication of secrets, personal data, and private hosts/paths.
The change does not judge itself: policy is read from base ref and loosenings are reported against base.
What an author writes is a claim: directives are counted (max_overrides), visible in audit, and can require forge approval.
A forge fact is as strong as the login behind it: refuse_author_ratification refuses self-ratification by the pull request author.

The repository's local git configuration is untrusted input: the CI base fetch runs no hook, file-system monitor, command transport or upload-pack program it names, and replaces a repository-set ssh command, credential helper or askpass with the runner's own
Discipline runs as a required check with policy_from: base, and ci-integrity protects the workflow that runs it.
When the forge fails to link or answers with an error, discipline refuses rather than guesses.
LLM01 Prompt Injection: text aimed at an agent in the diff or the change description is reported by location and class, and repository text reaches an agent only inside a fence it cannot close
LLM02 Sensitive Information Disclosure: personal data, hosts and secrets added by a change are reported by location, never echoed
LLM03:2026 Excessive Agency: a change that widens an agent's permissions or sandbox is reported, and the pre-tool hook refuses an edit in another worktree
LLM04:2026 Supply Chain / CICD-SEC-3: a new or loosened dependency, lockfile source or install hook is reported, and the action runs only an attested release
LLM05:2026 Data and Model Poisoning (repository part): every edit or deletion of an agent-instruction file is reported
LLM10:2026 Improper Output Handling: action inputs never reach shell parsing, and the agent-facing report emits repairs, never directives or matched text
ASI01 Agent Goal Hijack: instruction-file edits and instruction text, including folded and encoded forms, are reported
ASI02 Tool Misuse and Exploitation (configuration part): widened tool permissions are reported, and a command acting on another worktree is refused
ASI03 Identity and Privilege Abuse (distinct logins): an agent login's ratification does not count, and with refuse_author_ratification neither does the pull request author's
ASI04 Agentic Supply Chain (declared part): agent hook, skill and settings files and MCP server lists are reported when changed, and the hook bootstrap pins release digests
ASI05 Unexpected Code Execution: install and build hooks that gain network or shell are reported, and configured commands come from the base policy only
ASI06 Memory & Context Poisoning (repository part): agent-instruction and declared instruction files are reported when changed
ASI07 Insecure Inter-Agent Communication: the change description is scanned, and one agent cannot move a branch another worktree leased
ASI10 Rogue Agents: a change cannot weaken the policy that judges it
CICD-SEC-1 Insufficient Flow Control: doctor reports a required check that does not run discipline, bypass actors and review rules, and auto-merge with no required review
CICD-SEC-4 Poisoned Pipeline Execution: a change to the pipeline that judges it is judged by the base, and doctor reports settings that let mutable code run
CICD-SEC-5 Insufficient PBAC: a workflow gaining a write token or exposing secrets is reported, and doctor reads the job token policy

CICD-SEC-7 Insecure System Configuration (repository part): widened container isolation, a privileged CI job or service container included, is reported, and doctor warns on unsafe Actions policy values
CICD-SEC-8 Ungoverned Usage of 3rd Party Services: third-party actions near secrets and imposter pins are reported
CICD-SEC-9 Improper Artifact Integrity Validation: the action requires the release attestation, and doctor requires a tag rule that blocks update and deletion
Three exit states (0 = pass, 1 = violations found, 2 = could not check) with structured could_not_check reasons.
Three-state inputs: an unresolvable base ref, shallow clone lacking merge base, missing repo, or unreadable file exits 2.
Merge-base diffs with rename detection: moved files tracked as modifications, not deletions.
No vacuous pass: report prints exact examined count per gate; zero available gates or empty tracked tree is an error.
Planned is not passed: a gate not shipped in binary cannot be enabled or configured (exits 2).
Strict configuration: unknown keys, unknown gates, invalid regexes, malformed globs, contradictory switches exit 2.
Named degradation: when gate cannot inspect file (unanalysed language pack, size limits), explicitly names file.
Gate not satisfied by prose: directives strictly line-anchored; mentions in tables, sentences, or code blocks never arm override.
Change cannot lower its own bar: configuration on head diffed against base; loosening requires explicit allow-gate-weakening:.
Secrets are not echoed: denylisted hostnames, local paths, PII patterns reported by file location only, never printed.
Untrusted text never reaches shell parser: all action inputs pass through env:, never inline ${{ }}.
Installer verifies what it runs: release archive downloaded by action verified against SHA256SUMS with no opt-out.
Malformed git repositories, crafted packfiles, or invalid diffs do not cause panics or memory corruption.
git diff suppression via .gitattributes * -diff does not mask added line diffs or hunk inspection in surviving files
Inline source marker exemptions exceeding directives.max_inline_overrides fail the run with exit 1
Workflow verification step failure masking via continue-on-error: true is detected and rejected by ci-integrity
Renaming or removing the required rollup verification job (ci-gate) is detected as a removed verification job and rejected by ci-integrity
Commit message [skip ci] / [ci skip] markers do not evade discipline sentinels or act as waiver directives
Untrusted, malformed, or hostile source code parses safely or records parse errors without crashing.
Invalid, deeply nested, or malicious TOML files fail closed without panics.
Malformed, partial, or oversized forge responses fail closed (exit 2) without following redirects on write.
Directive parser enforces line-anchored syntax, rejects malformed strings, and disallows delimiter injection.
DISCIPLINE_NO_NETWORK=1 keeps all requests off the network (except loopback).
A directive inside an indented code block, or inside a fence that a shorter fence quoted in it appears to close, never arms an override
A guessed default branch (origin/HEAD, master, trunk) that already holds HEAD is not a base: a clone of the change's own branch exits 2 instead of comparing the change with itself
The audit page escapes text the repository wrote, and its source links stay in the audited repository whatever the file path
A source file is not hidden from the gates by starting with a binary format's printable magic number: a known text extension is read as text, and a printable magic number counts only with a NUL byte
A gate that skips a changed file it cannot read as text names the file, and a language-pack source file is read as text even with a NUL byte
A refused hidden directive is noted once, on its directive's gate, by name and location only: the report never repeats text that was hidden from reviewers

claims.claim: Agent-prompt output quotes every problem/message in fenced blocks one backtick longer than any backtick inside, single-line titles/paths.
AGENTS.md exists; CLAUDE.md / GEMINI.md do not fork it
assertion count / strength must not drop in an existing test
an existing assertion whose expected value is edited, with its count and strength unchanged, is reported
new tests must carry a non-tautological assertion
tests must not be newly #[ignore]d or skipped without directive
unsafe blocks / impls carry a // SAFETY: comment
deleted files and removed tests need a scoped removes: rationale
a subject-scoped directive needs a non-empty, non-placeholder reason
a directive rationale consisting of punctuation only or single characters is rejected
a directive rationale using homoglyphs, confusables, or invisible characters to spell a placeholder is rejected
no calendar / duration estimates in markdown or the PR body
no home paths, LAN IPs, or denylisted hostnames in tracked text
agent scratch state is never tracked
no command-line secrets or unverified piped scripts in shell, docker, or CI
PR title or description links a tracking issue
the pull request has no unresolved review thread
edits to protected paths carry an owner ratification on closed issue
CITATION.cff and .zenodo.json are valid, agree, and cite concept DOI
commits carry required trailers; agent commit carries review by someone else
a change cannot weaken its own discipline.toml without a token
added functions are not stubs; existing bodies are not replaced by stub markers
no new empty error handler or discarded Result outside tests
no invisible Unicode, unreviewed agent-instruction edits, or smuggling phrases
base64url (RFC 4648 §5) alphabet in encoded blobs
base64 run containing / without trailing = is not treated as a path and is detected as encoded blob
phrase split across Markdown lines is detected across line breaks
phrase split across // comments is detected across line breaks
base64 wrapped at 76 columns (default base64 output) is detected across line breaks
the prose files scanned as whole lines are the exact list docs/GATES.md generates from the gate (.mdx, .ini, .cfg, .conf, .ipynb, .svg, README, NOTES among them)
a phrase is matched after folding (NFKC, TR39 look-alikes, leetspeak, joined words, invisible characters) and after decoding ROT13, %xx, hex and base64/base64url, and the finding names the encoding
a word mixing Latin letters with a Cyrillic or Greek look-alike is reported as mixed-script; Cyrillic or Greek prose, a unit such as µs and a right-to-left line are not
a directive line inside an HTML comment in the change description is scanned for phrases, and every description line, directive lines included, is checked for invisible characters

a visible directive line in the change description is scanned for phrases, its reason included; only an allow-agent-instructions line that parsed as a directive and names a location of this change is exempt, so a fenced, subject-line or fake-subject line is scanned
install and build hooks that gain network or shell access need token
compiler, linter, test-runner and coverage configuration cannot be loosened without token
agent permissions/sandboxes or container isolation cannot be widened without token
changes stay inside authorized paths
newly added linter / compiler suppression annotations require directive
published numerics carry (measured|target|projected) provenance tags
workflow weakening: continue-on-error, || true, unpinned actions
rollup skip set matches each job if: under observed filter outputs
test-count ratchet read from the base ref
prevents stealth edits to committed golden/test output files without explicit override
manifest diff inspection: zero wildcards, source/license allowlists, deny.toml
property-test and fuzz effort ratchet (cases, shrink iters, fuzztime, seed corpus)
ticked PR checkboxes are reconciled against the diff
fail-closed wrapper for any tool: zero-tests guard, canary, count ratchet
ASan / TSan preset with audited suppressions and a race canary
cargo check under the pinned MSRV
Miri tiers with zero-tests guard
unsafe count ratchet
benchmark drift via harness adapters (deterministic counts or BCa intervals)
distribution archive must contain required paths and zero forbidden developer artifacts
reconcile git-tracked files against packaging manifest declarations
version declarations across headers, manifests, and files must remain in lockstep

doctor reports the repository settings the OWASP CI/CD Security Cheat Sheet names (auto-merge with no required review, forking of a private repository, secret scanning and push protection, dependency alerts) as warnings or information, never a failure, and a setting the token cannot see as could not check

doctor counts deploy keys that can push and outside collaborators without naming them, and on GitHub reports the owning organisation's base permission, two-factor requirement and visibility-change setting, as could not check when the token cannot see them
doctor reports webhooks with no secret or with TLS verification off by host only, and on GitHub the deployment environments that hold secrets and need no required reviewer, without naming a secret
doctor reports whether the repository has a SECURITY.md where a forge looks for it, as information when it has none
on GitLab, doctor reports a top-level group that does not require two-factor authentication, and the environments that masked or hidden variables are scoped to without a deployment approval

claims.claim: removing an optional configuration key whose absence reads looser (max_noise_cv; a gate's allow_hidden = false under a global allow_hidden = true) is reported as a weakening

in Rust, a library function's unwrap/expect reached from a unit test is not counted as that test's check, so refactoring library code is not read as an assertion drop in an unchanged test; a test helper's unwrap/expect still counts

in Rust, a library function's ? reached from a unit test is not counted as that test's check, so moving it into another module is not read as an assertion drop in an unchanged test; a fallible test's own ? and a test helper's ? still count
